question: Who among the following social reformers wrote Brahmo Covenant which was a statement of the creed of the Brahmo Samaj?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Debendranath Tagore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Debendranath Tagore** was a prominent leader of the Brahmo Samaj and a key figure in the Bengal Renaissance.
 
• He authored the **Brahmo Covenant**, which is a statement of the creed of the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• Debendranath Tagore was instrumental in the development and propagation of **Brahmoism**, a reformist movement within Hinduism.
 
• He was the father of Rabindranath Tagore, the renowned poet and Nobel laureate.
 
• His contributions significantly shaped the religious and social reform movements in 19th century India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmo Samaj**:

 
 
• Founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828, it aimed at reforming the social and religious practices of Hindu society.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj advocated for monotheism and rejected the caste system and idol worship.
 
 
 
• **Keshab Chandra Sen**:
 
 
• He was a prominent Indian social reformer who joined the Brahmo Samaj in 1857.
 
• Sen later founded his own sect, the Brahmo Samaj of India, in 1866.
 
 
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**:
 
 
• He is considered the father of the Indian Renaissance and was the founder of the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• Roy campaigned against social evils like Sati and child marriage.
 
 
 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**:
 
 
• He was a key figure in the Bengal Renaissance and worked for the upliftment of women and education reforms.
 
• Vidyasagar played a significant role in the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856.
